tagline: South Korea's southwestern art city is famous for its democracy movement, the Gwangju Biennale and some of the richest food in the country, beneath Mudeungsan National Park.
overview: Gwangju is the largest city in Korea's southwest and the capital of the Jeolla region's culture. It is closely tied to the May 18 Democratic Uprising of 1980, when citizens rose up against military rule; the movement is remembered at the May 18th National Cemetery and the 5·18 Memorial Park.

Art is central here. The Gwangju Biennale, founded in 1995, was Asia's first contemporary art biennale, and the Asia Culture Center in the old provincial office area is one of the largest cultural complexes in Asia. Penguin Village and Yangnim-dong's old missionary houses make good walks.

Jeolla cooking is famous across Korea for its many side dishes, and Gwangju's tteokgalbi, grilled minced rib patties, is a local signature. Mudeungsan National Park rises right at the city's edge, with its basalt column cliffs and autumn colour.
